items.publisher: Reuters / U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
items.headline: July PPI is flat, easing the immediate wholesale-inflation shock
items.summary: U.S. producer prices were unchanged in July after a revised June decline. Final-demand goods prices fell while services rose modestly; the year-over-year rate slowed from June. The result was softer than consensus and reduces the immediate inflation surprise risk, although late-July oil spikes are not fully captured.
items.whyItMatters: CPI and PPI now both argue against a fresh near-term inflation acceleration, but core PCE, energy and long-duration yields still matter for the September Fed decision and equity multiples.

items.headline: AI financing is becoming a credit-market risk, not only an equity-capex story
items.summary: Barron's highlights the rapid institutionalization of AI infrastructure finance: Nvidia is working with major Wall Street firms to mobilize roughly USD 500 billion, while structures backed by chips and data-center assets could evolve into securitized products. The opportunity is real, but leverage, collateral values and obsolescence now become part of the AI risk map.
items.whyItMatters: The AI cycle is migrating from corporate capex into private credit, leasing and potentially securitized debt. If utilization, productivity or residual chip values disappoint, losses could transmit beyond technology equities into credit markets and financial institutions.

items.headline: Cisco validates broadening AI infrastructure demand beyond GPUs
items.summary: Cisco reported fiscal fourth-quarter adjusted EPS and revenue above expectations, with networking revenue rising strongly and fiscal-year AI infrastructure orders from hyperscalers reaching roughly USD 9.3 billion. Management also guided fiscal 2027 revenue and earnings above prior market expectations.
items.whyItMatters: AI spending is broadening into networking, switching and connectivity. This supports the thesis that the buildout has multiple beneficiaries, while Cisco's margin pressure shows component inflation and hardware mix still matter.

items.headline: July U.S. budget deficit reopens the long-duration fiscal-risk discussion
items.summary: Barron's flagged a five-year high for the July monthly U.S. budget deficit, reversing recent improvement. The signal is material because elevated borrowing needs coincide with Treasury yields already near multi-decade highs.
items.whyItMatters: Persistent fiscal deficits can keep term premia and long yields elevated even if monthly inflation cools, limiting the valuation benefit from softer CPI/PPI and keeping real-estate refinancing costs sticky.

items.headline: Softer inflation supports risk assets, but the curve and oil keep policy uncertainty alive
items.summary: Markets received the July CPI constructively and the July PPI was also soft, but long Treasury yields remain elevated and oil risks are not fully reflected in the latest inflation prints. The near-term macro signal improved without resolving the medium-term duration problem.
items.whyItMatters: A benign inflation print can support equities while long yields stay restrictive. AGCI therefore separates tactical relief from a durable change in the cost-of-capital regime.
